name: Missouri
summary: Statutes and constitution: revisor.mo.gov (unofficial, uncertified) serves one section per constructible URL and reads cleanly with fetch_doc.py; WebFetch is gated on built URLs, and Justia's 2025 RSMo is the tier-2 fallback. Court rules: official per-rule pages on courts.mo.gov have opaque ids (WebFetch reads them, the script gets 403); the courts' Clerk Handbooks Domino database offers a GET search the script can read. CSR and Missouri Register are long two-column PDFs on sos.mo.gov (script ok); LII mirrors the CSR per rule. Case law: courts.mo.gov opinion PDFs refuse the script (403) and error in WebFetch, so Justia (constructible by docket and year) is the quoting route; Supreme Court minutes (Domino, script ok, from 1998) give hand-downs and transfer dispositions by Court of Appeals docket.

citation_map.notes: Missouri style cites sections as 'section 516.120, RSMo 2016' or 'RSMo Cum. Supp. 2024', with subsections in dotted form (537.765.3) - trim to chapter.section for URLs. Bare 'section 516.120' (no RSMo) is context_required: chapter.section numbering is shared with other states (e.g. Minn. Stat. 609.75). Court rules are cited 'Rule 55.27(a)(6)' with no state marker (context_required); Rule 4 professional-conduct rules are cited 'Rule 4-1.7', the same shape as Florida Bar rules, so bare forms route only with Missouri context. Missouri parentheticals: '(Mo. banc 2022)' for the Supreme Court en banc, '(Mo. App. E.D. 2023)' (Missouri style) or '(Mo. Ct. App. 2023)' (Bluebook) for the Court of Appeals. No public-domain citation. Dockets: SC##### (Supreme Court), ED/WD/SD##### (Court of Appeals districts). Subsequent history 'transfer denied' is shared with other states' usage, so context_required. Supreme Court reports 'Mo.' ended 1956 and 'Mo. App.' 1952 (from memory). CourtListener ids from memory, unverified. A '§§ 516.110-516.120' range is two sections: the regex takes the first.

sources.coverage: All chapters of RSMo, current text with effective date, history, prior revisions and annotations; future-effective and multiply-enacted versions listed under 'All versions'.

access.pattern_rules: {section} = chapter.section exactly as cited (516.120, 537.765, 56.067); no title or padding. Drop Missouri-style subsection suffixes before building ('537.765.3' -> 537.765; subsection 3 is in the body). Chapter page: /main/PageSelect.aspx?chapter={chapter}. Where a section has several versions (multiply enacted, future effective, or held unconstitutional) the page shows one version and an 'All versions' table whose PageSelect.aspx?section={section}&bid={bid} links open each version.

automation.robots_txt: no robots file: /robots.txt redirects to an HTML 'Object Moved' page -> Home.aspx (no rules); fetch_doc.py check: robots permits
automation.notes: WebFetch on a built OneSection URL (537.765) was held for a permission prompt that went unanswered (PROVENANCE_REQUIRED); use fetch_doc.py. Pages are small (7-11K chars). Help page says the site programmatically slows down 'malicious access'; the script's 1.1 s spacing was fine.
